conceptZh: 橡膠恐龍為了吃咖喱飯把自己彈射出去，飛過目標撞上軟牆、倒栽進飯桶，震落的零件排成「歐」，最後用尾巴舀飯吃。
object: A springboard-mounted rubber dinosaur and a curry-rice bucket beneath a padded glyph-parts rack.
morph: The rebound shakes loose saturated blue pieces from a padded rack; they fall into a precise frontal Traditional Chinese 歐, with 區 on the left and 欠 on the right.
creativeAngle: 把瑪利歐設定為原創橡膠恐龍的名字，以吃咖喱飯呼應家長方向，完全不用既有角色造型；短手搆不到飯，才引發全身彈射與倒栽桶的笑點。
promptEn:
Create an 8-second stylized toy animation in a fixed frontal wide shot, on a pale warm-peach set. The original mint-green rubber dinosaur has enormous feet, absurdly tiny arms, and stubborn confidence. Its personal name is 瑪利歐; give it a completely original dinosaur design. A springboard and a curry-rice bucket beside a padded backstop form one simple launch setup. Behind the action, a shallow rack holds saturated cobalt-blue glyph components. Keep the central teaching area unobstructed.

0.0–1.4 seconds: The dinosaur eyes the curry rice, stretches both tiny arms, and misses the bucket by a ridiculous distance. Determined, it belly-flops onto the springboard, feet raised in a drumroll pose. Its weight depresses the board and starts loosening the rack. At 0.5 seconds the off-screen voice says the first “歐”; a blue component visibly tips as construction begins.

1.4–3.2 seconds: The dinosaur silently counts down with three emphatic foot bobs. BOING: the board launches its whole rubber body in a huge left-to-right arc. It sails straight past the rice, eyes tracking the missed meal while its useless little arms keep reaching. Keep the complete flight visible.

3.2–5.0 seconds: A soft BONK against the padded far side squashes its snout, rebounds it backward, and drops it upside-down into the bucket, enormous feet bicycling overhead. That single impact shakes the rack: the blue pieces tumble down short guided tracks into the exact glyph 歐. Use a correctly drawn Traditional Chinese glyph template for every piece and final placement: 區 at left, its three distinct 口 openings clear, and 欠 at right. At 4.6 seconds, as the final piece seats, the voice says the second “歐”.

5.0–8.0 seconds: Hold the completed 歐 perfectly still, centered, uncropped, approximately 70% of frame height with generous margins. Below and clear of its strokes, the dinosaur wriggles upright in its bucket. At 5.8 seconds, as the voice says “瑪利歐”, this named dinosaur uses its flexible spoon-shaped tail to scoop a clearly visible mouthful of curry rice, eats it, and happily wiggles its feet.

Warm, friendly off-screen Taiwanese Mandarin, exact spoken line: “歐、歐、瑪利歐” (ㄡ、ㄡ、ㄇㄚˇ ㄌㄧˋ ㄡ). Read exactly these syllables slowly and distinctly with clear tones, then stop. Gentle rubber squeaks and a soft spring sound support the voice. Only 歐 appears as text; no captions, logos, watermarks, extra dialogue, flashing, or background clutter.
